reproducibility_header: OH WITHIN-STATE COUNTY-GRAIN TEST v1. Built 2026-11-23 from oh_county_mh_v1.jsonl (LSC per-county state-MH dollars, FY2019-FY2026, all-88-county sums reconcile to LSC statewide table within ±5 USD FY19-24 and delta-0 FY25-26; Hamilton delta-0 vs banked for the FY22-25 verified class) and oh_county_crime_v1.jsonl (FBI CDE per-agency HOM monthly counts, 823 OH ORIs, months-present guard layered all-agencies vs core city+sheriff). Population denominators: Census PEP SUMLEV-050 county estimates (vintage-2019 for CY2019; vintage-2025 for CY2020-2025). FY-vs-CY alignment law: LSC Ohio FY runs Jul(t-1)-Jun(t); pairs are matched MH fiscal-year t to murder calendar-year t+lag where lag 0 = overlapping window, lag 1/t+1 and lag 2/t+2 = post-spending windows. Pooled = all county-years; within-county-demeaned = each county's MH and murder-rate series demeaned before pooling (removes the cross-county level effect; tests only within-county co-movement). Big-county separate reads = the six CIN/Franklin-Columbus/Cuyahoga-Cleveland/Montgomery-Dayton/Lucas-Toledo/Summit-Akron-class counties. OOH check = split-half honest holdout (train 2019-2021, test 2022-2024) at the pooled level. No fabrication: every input row traceable to a downloaded PDF or CDE call; nulls = route-absent, never zeros.
alignment_note: LSC fiscal year Jul(t-1)-Jun(t); crime calendar year. t+lag on the crime year: lag0=FY t overlaps CY t (6-month overlap), lag1=CY t+1 fully post-FY, lag2=CY t+2.

metric_definitions.mh_usd_per_100k: LSC county total state-MH dollars (subsidy+capital verified) / PEP county pop * 100k, same-year CY pop vs FY label (flagged: FY mid-year at Jun 30; CY pop at Jul 1)
metric_definitions.murder_rate_per_100k_core: CDE sum of homicide monthly counts, City+County agencies only / PEP county pop * 100k
metric_definitions.murder_rate_per_100k_all: same across all 823 reporting agencies incl. university/park/special-district

ooh_check.design: pooled county-year split-half: train CY2019-2021, honest holdout CY2022-2024
ooh_check.note: holdout direction matches train (+) but both are r<0.09 — no exploitable signal; holdout honesty preserved (no peeking, no tuning).

verdict.pooled_88: NULL-TO-FAINT-POSITIVE: pooled Pearson r = +0.05 (lag0), +0.05 (lag1), +0.06 (lag2); Spearman rho = +0.20 on all three lags. The rho/pearson gap means the rank association is monotone-positive across counties (higher-MH counties marginally higher murder rates) but any linear read is swamped by county scale differences.
verdict.within_county_demeaned: EFFECTIVELY NULL: r = -0.01/-0.02/+0.03, rho = +0.04/+0.02/+0.06. Removing county fixed means, there is NO within-county co-movement between state-MH dollars per capita and murder rates in any lag direction.
verdict.big_county_reads: HETEROGENEOUS AND SMALL-N (7 county-years each): Franklin-Columbus lag1/lag2 NEGATIVE (r -0.43/-0.62; biggest MH surge FY22 $6.7M/100k followed by rate 17.4 -> 7.2), Cuyahoga-Cleveland lag1 NEGATIVE (r -0.74), Hamilton-Cincinnati lag1 POSITIVE (r +0.92), Lucas-Toledo lag1 POSITIVE (+0.55), Montgomery-Dayton lag0 NEGATIVE (-0.64), Summit-Akron mixed. n=5-7 makes every one of these fragile; no consistent direction across the six.
verdict.oh_check_verdict: OOH same-sign but trivial magnitude both halves — the pooled faint positive does not survive as a predictive relationship.
verdict.bottom_line: At county grain WITHIN Ohio, state-MH spending per capita shows no reliable pooled or within-county association with murder rates at t, t+1, or t+2. The only structured signals are negative lag1/lag2 co-movements in the two largest counties (Franklin, Cuyahoga) — consistent with the prior city-grain findings' direction but far from conclusive at n=7 each. NULL IS THE HONEST HEADLINE.
